title: Extracorporeal shock wave therapy for the treatment of ganglions of the hand
summary:
Background:
Ganglion cysts of the hand and wrist are the most common soft tissue tumors in this area. They often develop as sacs in the joint capsule or tendon sheaths and are sometimes associated with functional limitations of the hand. The most common location is the extensor side of the wrist. Women between the ages of 20 and 30 are three times more likely to be affected than men.  Treatment depends on the severity of the patient's symptoms, although spontaneous regression has also been reported. In cases of functional impairment and pain, a release puncture or surgical intervention may be performed. Focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) uses special acoustic waves to initiate regenerative processes via induced mechanotransduction and activated cellular signaling pathways.
Research question:
A recently published case report described the successful treatment of a ganglion with ESWT for the first time. Further studies on the effect of focused ESWT on ganglions of the hand are lacking. This raises the question of whether the positive effect found can also be demonstrated in a larger study and control group design.
Methodology:
First, all study participants undergo an examination including ultrasound diagnosis and collection of study-relevant data by means of an intake interview
and their own and standardized questionnaires. The study is then divided into an intervention and a control group. 
In the intervention group, study participants receive three shock wave treatments at weekly intervals at the Institute for Physical and Rehabilitative Medicine at the UKJ. Following the last treatment, a 12-week waiting period begins, after which a new examination and diagnosis takes place, including ultrasound and questionnaire completion. The control group will not receive any intervention and will have a 12-week waiting period between the first measurement at the beginning of the study and the end of the study in order to observe any spontaneous decline.
conditions: Ganglion cyst on the extensor side of the wrist

interventions.name:
Intervention group:
-Sonographic examination of the ganglion, completion of questionnaires (DASH; SF-12 and our own questionnaire on pain symptoms, other therapies, and ability to work)
-first shock wave appointment, 15 min: ESWT treatment (week 1)
-Second shock wave appointment, 15 min: ESWT tre

Control group:
-Sonographic examination of the ganglion, completion of questionnaires (DASH; SF-12 and our own questionnaire on pain symptoms, further therapies, and ability to work)
-Follow-up appointment after 12 weeks, repeat sonographic examination of the ganglion, completion of questionnaires

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Sonographic evidence of a ganglion on the extensor side of the wrist
• Written patient consent to participate in the study (informed consent)
Exclusion criteria:
• Previous ESWT on the affected hand within the last 12 months
• Malignant tumor processes in the treatment area
• Skin defects in the treatment area
• Severe psychiatric illness
• Legal guardianship in medical matters by third parties
